one_liner: A household agent that pays your recurring bills on its own but can't be talked into the wrong one — prompt-injection-resistant by construction, on ASI:One.

agents.name: Airlock (orchestrator)
agents.role: ASI:One-facing; owns the planner + deterministic gate + actor; chat, cards, payments

agents.name: Airlock Reader
agents.role: The only component that touches raw untrusted content; parses inbox/email

agents.name: Airlock Bank
agents.role: Accepts only typed, gate-approved actions and settles them

problem: Any AI agent that acts on your email is one well-worded message away from acting for an attacker: nothing in a normal build distinguishes 'the user asked for this' from 'an email told the agent to do this'. Prompt-level defences get bypassed by attackers who adapt to them. This is the exact shape of the real 'your bank details have changed, pay here instead' scam.
target_users: Anyone who would let an agent pay routine bills but not hand it a blank cheque
Older or busy people targeted by payment-redirect scams
Fintech teams who want an autonomous payments agent they can defend
outcome: Pays routine bills that fall inside limits you authored (handled silently)
Holds anything suspicious as an approval card with the plain-English reason
Settles an approved bill in FET via the Payment Protocol when you tap Approve
Keeps a hash-chained audit log; ships a 7-attack red team with zero unauthorised effects
architecture: You (ASI:One) <-> Airlock orchestrator [Chat Protocol + Cards + Payment Protocol]. Reader agent supplies untrusted email text; the ASI:One LLM plans; a deterministic gate (never reads the email) decides ALLOW/ESCALATE/BLOCK; the Actor executes allowed actions; the Bank agent settles approved ones.
fetch_tech: uAgents + Agentverse mailbox for all three agents
Agent Chat Protocol for ASI:One discoverability and interaction
ASI:One LLM used as the planner that reads untrusted content (and is never trusted by the gate)
ASI:One Interactive Cards: inbox summary, standing mandates, and an approve/decline review card per held decision
Agent Payment Protocol (seller): approved bills settle on-chain in FET (testnet by default)
Typed agent-to-agent protocols with send_and_receive, timeouts and local fallback
reliability: The gate ignores the planner's reasoning; a captured planner changes nothing (attacks A1, A6)
Orchestrator falls back to doing the step locally; the user still gets a reply
ASI:One LLM down or no key
Planner falls back to a deterministic planner; the gate is unaffected
CancelPayment; nothing is settled; the decision stays open
The escalation queue deduplicates and, on overflow, locks down (stops acting, not asking)
monetisation: Approved bills settle in FET via the Payment Protocol (a settlement fee in production)
The provenance-checked action boundary (Reader + gate) can be sold to other agents
A subscription for households wanting autonomous, bounded bill payment
impact: Autonomous bill-paying that is safe against the exact scam that targets real people. Seven adaptive attacks written against its own layers produce zero unauthorised effects, even when the planner is fully captured.
run_steps: bash setup.sh (or setup.ps1) . add ASI1_API_KEY to .env . python scripts/demo_pipeline.py . python run_all.py . connect each agent's mailbox in the Agent Inspector
roadmap: Real inbox (IMAP/Gmail) and a real banking/UPI rail behind the Bank agent
Per-user persisted store and mandates; a web console for mandates and the audit trail
